title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: 'Fear Factory' Lanny Manson
how: Defeated Ma Porter via submission in the DPW/ICW Women's World Championship Tournament Finals at the Oakland Coliseum, Oakland, California.
note: The fed's own ledger records this as two entries — the tournament final of 5 April 1996 under the two federations GDWA grew out of, and her inauguration as GDWA World Champion at the same building on 21 April 1996, the day the promotion opened. They are one reign, and the second entry is the fed dating its own founding on its own title ledger.

title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: Zaranna
how: Defeated 'Fear Factory' Lanny Manson via pinfall at the Summer Supercard pay per view, Tacoma Dome, Tacoma, Washington.
note: Stripped of the World Title due to contract breachment on 20 July 1996, in the GDWA front offices in Walnut Creek, California. The belt stood vacant until the October tournament.

title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: Andrea Chandler
how: Defeated 'Fear Factory' Lanny Manson via pinfall in the finals of the World Championship Tournament at the Fukuoka Dome, Fukuoka, Japan.
note: The fed's own Wrestler of the Month citations credit her with holding the title five months undefeated through January and February 1997.

title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: Dementia Praecox
how: Defeated Andrea Chandler via pinfall at the Founder's Day Tradition pay per view, Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio.

title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: Officer Order
how: Defeated Dementia Praecox and Sierra Browne in a Three Way Dance, by pinfall and disqualification respectively, at the Oakland Coliseum Arena, Oakland, California.

title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: Medusa Rage
how: Defeated Officer Order via pinfall at the Oakland Coliseum, Oakland, California.

title: gdwa-world-heavyweight
label: Black Lotus
how: Defeated Medusa Rage via submission in a Scientific Submission rules match at the Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio, during the Founder's Day Tradition II pay per view.
note: The last World Heavyweight change the fed's own ledger records.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Dangerous Queen' Sachie Yokoyama
how: Last-eliminated 'Jungle' Radhi Ananda in the Western Heritage Championship Royal Rumble at the Summer Supercard pay per view, Tacoma Dome, Tacoma, Washington, to become the inaugural champion.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: Officer Order
how: Defeated 'The Dangerous Queen' Sachie Yokoyama via pinfall at The Spectrum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Dangerous Queen' Sachie Yokoyama (2)
how: Knocked Officer Order out at the Fall Moonsault pay per view, Carolinas Stadium, Charlotte, North Carolina.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Jungle' Radhi Ananda
how: Defeated 'The Dangerous Queen' Sachie Yokoyama via pinfall at the Cow Palace, San Francisco, California.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: Officer Order (2)
how: Defeated 'Jungle' Radhi Ananda via pinfall at the Founder's Day Tradition pay per view, Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio.
note: The fed's own ledger dates this Founder's Day Tradition title change 21 March 1997 and the World title change on the same card 17 March 1997. Both stand as written; the pay-per-view calendar bills the inaugural Founders' Day Tradition for 24 February 1997, a third date. The disagreement is recorded, not resolved.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Golden Girl' Sierra Browne
how: Defeated Officer Order via pinfall at Market Square Arena, Indianapolis, Indiana — the first time any wrestler in the fed held two of its championships at once.
note: The fed's own card (Tuesday Night Catfight billed Tuesday 15 April 1997, Market Square Arena, Indianapolis, 19,125) bills this exact title change — Sierra Browne over Officer Order — at the identical venue, three weeks before the Lineages page's own 5 May 1997 date for it.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Kyoto Crippler' Keiko Mita
how: Last-eliminated 'Yukon' Jane in the Western Heritage Royal Rumble at Fall Moonsault 1997, Sky Dome, Toronto, Canada.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Jungle' Radhi Ananda (2)
how: Defeated 'Kyoto Crippler' Keiko Mita via pinfall at the Key Arena, Seattle, Washington.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Golden Girl' Sierra Browne (2)
how: Defeated 'Jungle' Radhi Ananda via pinfall at the Pittsburgh Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
note: Won and lost on the same date at the same building, per the fed's own ledger, which records her as a two-time multi-titled champion for it.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'La Femme Nikita' Nikita Marx
how: Defeated 'Golden Girl' Sierra Browne in a "Throw in the Towel" match at the Pittsburgh Civic Arena, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: 'Ultima' Sarah Summers
how: Defeated 'La Femme Nikita' Nikita Marx via submission at the Palace in Auburn Hills, Michigan.

title: gdwa-western-heritage
label: Daisy Butterfly
how: Defeated 'Ultima' Sarah Summers via submission at the Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio, during Founder's Day Tradition II, unifying the Western Heritage and Intercontinental championships.
note: The fed's own handler's page of 21 October 2000 announces a brand new Western Heritage Champion three days out, from its first card out of Tacoma; nothing held records who won it, or what happened to this reign in between.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Demonica
how: Defeated Valkyrie via pinfall in the GDWA Internet Championship Tournament Finals at the Summer Supercard pay per view, Tacoma Dome, Tacoma, Washington.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Charlotte La Mancha
how: Defeated Demonica via submission at the Rose Garden, Portland, Oregon.
note: Stripped due to contract breachment on 4 February 1997, in the GDWA front offices in Walnut Creek, California.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Staci X
how: Last-eliminated Medusa Rage in the Internet Heavyweight Championship Royal Rumble at the Key Arena, Seattle, Washington.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Dementia Praecox
how: Defeated Staci X via submission at the Cow Palace, San Francisco, California.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: 'Legend' Micki Duran
how: Defeated Dementia Praecox via pinfall at the Founder's Day Tradition pay per view, Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Daisy Butterfly
how: Defeated Micki Duran via submission at the Cow Palace, San Francisco, California.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Sierra Browne
how: Defeated Daisy Butterfly via pinfall at the Great Western Forum, Los Angeles, California — the fed's own first tri-titled champion.

title: gdwa-internet-heavyweight
label: Daisy Butterfly (2)
how: Defeated Micki Duran and Sierra Brown in a Three Way Dance at Fall Moonsault 1997, Sky Dome, Toronto, Canada.
note: The reign carried on unbroken into the renamed belt: on 18 January 1998 in Sendai the fed formally changed the title from the Internet Heavyweight Championship to the Intercontinental Championship, with the same holder.

title: gdwa-intercontinental
label: Daisy Butterfly
how: Inaugurated as GDWA Intercontinental champion at the Miyagi-ken Sports Center in Sendai, Japan, when the fed formally changed the title's name from the Internet Heavyweight Championship.
note: The reign carried over unbroken from the Internet Heavyweight Championship she had held since 10 November 1997. It ended in the match that unified this title with the Western Heritage Championship at Founder's Day Tradition II, which she won.

title: gdwa-transnational-cruiserweight
label: 'Golden Girl' Sierra Browne
how: Defeated 'Kyoto Crippler' Keiko Mita via pinfall in the Cruiserweight Championship Tournament Finals at the US Air Arena, Baltimore, Maryland, to become the inaugural champion.
note: "The Cruiserweight title is vacated on August 30, 1998 at the Municipal Stadium in Cleveland, Ohio during the Founder's Day Tradition II pay per view" — the fed's own lineage, which records no holder between this reign and the vacancy. The fed announced a tournament to crown a new Cruiserweight champion for January 2000.

title: gdwa-american-heritage
label: Daisy Butterfly
how: Defeated 'Ultima' Sarah Summers via submission at the Municipal Stadium, Cleveland, Ohio, during Founder's Day Tradition II, unifying the Western Heritage and Intercontinental championships, and was crowned the inaugural American Heritage Champion.
note: The only American Heritage reign the fed's own ledger records; it files the title among its retired heavyweight championships.

title: gdwa-world-tag-team
label: Misfits
how: Defeated Lady Luck via pinfall in Osaka Castle Hall, Osaka, Japan, to become the inaugural champions.

title: gdwa-world-tag-team
label: The Hyena Queens
how: Defeated the Misfits by exiting the steel cage, in Madison Square Garden, New York City, New York.
note: Stripped of the World Tag Team titles after the fed held its own tag division up, on 26 September 1997 in the GDWA offices in Walnut Creek, California.

title: gdwa-ironwoman
label: 'The Franchise' Daisy Butterfly
how: Crowned Ironwoman at the Fall Moonsault pay per view, Carolinas Stadium, Charlotte, North Carolina.
note: The crowning is contested once a year rather than defended; the closing date is the night the next Ironwoman was crowned.

title: gdwa-ironwoman
label: Andrea Chandler
how: Crowned Ironwoman at the Fall Moonsault 1997 pay per view, Sky Dome, Toronto, Canada.
note: The fed named her Wrestler of the Month for November and December 1997 for winning it.

title: gdwa-extreme-television
label: Heidi Leick

won.source: the fed's own Tease and Catfight, 30 December 1998 (msg_id e7ZLH3O5EXIJ; promotions/gdwa/archive/gdwa-tease-and-catfight-1998-12-30.html)

how: Awarded the newly created title outright by the front office, with no match; defended it the same night with a pinfall (Diamond Cutter) over debuting Caitlin Nevon.

title: gdwa-ladies-extreme-tag-team
label: Misfits

won.source: the fed's own Tuesday Night Catfight, billed 22 July 1997 (msg_id BWv_zvdAyBYJ and 5 more; promotions/gdwa/archive/gdwa-tuesday-night-catfight-1997-07-22.html), introducing Dalbello Rage as one half of the champions; the deciding tournament match is not in this held record, only the broadcast's own championship billing

how: Won the fed's own Ladies Extreme tag tournament (bracket announced 7 July 1997); the deciding match itself is not shown.
